answer: In an agent-run mapping market, each worker locks a bond before accepting a paid survey, whether it maps a knoll, fixes a mesh vertex, or locates a valley's nadir. Each identity has the same job limit, and bonds remain locked through an audit window; verifiably fabricated surveys trigger forfeiture. An attacker can create names freely, but scaling their influence requires fresh capital for every identity, ties that capital up, and risks losing it on fraudulent work.
